chunk_findings.detail: `test_show_reports_the_phase_needs_a_task_inherits` reads `json.loads(out)["needs"]`, but `show` in `ddflow/api/reporting/records.py` puts the patched field under `item` (`O.ok(..., item={**shown, ...})` with `shown["needs"]`). For the fixture task `P1.T1`, the JSON has no top-level `needs`, so the assertion raises `KeyError` on both the unfixed and fixed code and never checks `item["needs"] == ["P0"]`. The show half of B8981fa81bd is therefore untested; a regression that still omits inherited phase needs inside `item` would not be caught by this test.

data.probe: CLI ddflow --json show TASK flattens O.ok(item={...}) to top-level keys. tests/test_list_show_inherited_needs.py::test_show_reports_the_phase_needs_a_task_inherits reads run_cli --json show P1.T1 then json.loads(out)['needs'], the patched top-level shown['needs'] (running ddflow --json show fix-B8981fa81bd has needs at the TOP level, no item wrapper). Unfixed it reports [] and [] == ['P0'] fails exactly as test_task_list_reports_the_phase_needs_a_task_inherits does; fixed it reports ['P0'] and the CI selected run passes.
